problem:
Consider the set $B,$ defined as

$$
B={\frac{1}{n+6}:n\in {\pm 1,\pm 2}}.
$$

Which of the following sets is equivalent to $B?$
worked_solution:
The elements of $B$ are all the terms of the sequence ${b}_{n},$ given by

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{1}{n+6},\,n\in {-2,-1,1,2}.
$$

Let's write down all the terms of our sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} & =\frac{1}{(-2)+6}=\frac{1}{4} \\ {b}_{2} & =\frac{1}{(-1)+6}=\frac{1}{5} \\ {b}_{3} & =\frac{1}{1+6}=\frac{1}{7} \\ {b}_{4} & =\frac{1}{2+6}=\frac{1}{8}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
B={\frac{1}{4},\frac{1}{5},\frac{1}{7},\frac{1}{8}}.
$$
